title: Listen to the Grand Ole Opry’s Saturday Night Show Dedicated to Dolly Parton
summary: SiriusXM is paying tribute to the legendary singer, songwriter, and actress who died at the age of 80.
body_markdown:
The Dolly Parton Tribute Channel celebrated the life, music, and legacy of[Dolly Parton](https://www.siriusxm.com/blog/tag/dolly-parton) with her career-spanning music, exclusive stories, and tributes from across SiriusXM.


Fans can continue the celebration by listening to the Grand Ole Opry’s Saturday Night Show dedicated to Dolly Parton on the SiriusXM app until Monday, September 7.


### **Listen to the Grand Ole Opry’s Saturday Night Show Dedicated to Dolly Parton**


The Grand Ole Opry dedicated its Saturday night show to Country Music Hall of Fame and Grand Ole Opry Member Dolly Parton, honoring her life, legacy, and contributions to country music.


Listen to the special show on demand in the SiriusXM app until Monday, September 7.


Carly Pearce and Jelly Roll performing “9 to 5” at the Grand Ole Opry’s Dolly Parton Tribute. (Credit: Mark Mosrie)


The show originally aired live Saturday, August 29 at 9pm ET on The Dolly Parton Tribute Channel (Ch. 105) and[Willie’s Roadhouse (Ch. 61)](https://www.siriusxm.com/blog/tag/willies-roadhouse) .


Carly Pearce, who began her career at Dollywood and was surprised by Parton with an invitation to become an official Grand Ole Opry member in 2021, and surprise guest Jelly Roll were among the artists who appeared in the tribute.


#### **Grand Ole Opry Dolly Parton Tribute Lineup**


- Carly Pearce
- Jelly Roll
- Kathy Mattea
- Molly Tuttle
- T. Graham Brown
- Channing Wilson
- Belle Frantz
- Jada Star
- Dan Tyminski
- Opry Band + Opry Square Dancers


### **The Dolly Parton Tribute Channel on SiriusXM**


The limited-run Dolly Parton Tribute Channel featured Dolly’s career-spanning music, exclusive stories, hand-picked favorite songs, and tributes celebrating her extraordinary life and career. The channel launched August 25 at 8pm ET with a live call-in show hosted by Cody Alan.


The Queen of Country and pop-culture icon passed away Tuesday, August 25 at the age of 80, her family said in a statement.


Throughout her remarkable seven-decade career, Parton became one of the most beloved and influential artists in music history, writing and singing enduring classics including “Jolene,” “9 to 5,” and “I Will Always Love You.” She was inducted into both the Country Music Hall of Fame and Rock & Roll Hall of Fame and won 11 Grammy Awards as well as the Recording Academy’s Lifetime Achievement Award.
